submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad copy/retrieval head: at a token it puts near-exclusive attention (weight 0.9-1.0) on one earlier token - the delimiter that just opened the bracket/quote it sits inside, a numeral/operator token, a word-initial content word, or a non-ASCII script fragment - and writes that token's layer-4 value into the residual stream, so its strength is the value-novelty of the copied token (measured strength equals that key's value distance with median error 0.00 whenever the top weight exceeds 0.95) and exactly 0 whenever attention stays on the position-0 sink. Predict active on any text containing non-Latin script (21/21 scripted passages at 1.28-2.06 and 7/8 short English sentences carrying one non-Latin word at 0.70-1.64; scan rates: Chinese 52%, Japanese 47%, Arabic 34% of tokens vs English 14%) and on code/arithmetic tokens inside a just-opened bracket or after a fresh operator (8/10 code lines and 4/5 arithmetic lines at 0.43-2.39); predict plain ASCII English prose active-weak (per-text peak 0.3-1.0: 4/15 single sentences and 4/5 two-sentence passages over the 0.652 line), and predict exactly 0 only for a flat list of common English words or plain integers and for two-token texts such as 'Yes.' (53/53 measured at 0.00; lists that contain a distinctive word such as 'otter' or 'wednesday' instead reached 0.78-0.85), where attention never leaves the sink.

rival_explanations: Narrower reading: this is only an opening-delimiter copy head, so it should fire on tokens inside a just-opened bracket, quote or keyword clause and stay near zero on non-Latin prose, which has no such delimiters.

Mechanism-free reading: the write tracks the current token's own rarity or surprisal (a token-frequency effect), so firing should follow the query token's identity and ignore which earlier token is attended.

Sibling reading: like L4/H4 this is a sentence-boundary topic/name copier, so it should fire at periods, commas and newlines only when a salient proper name or topic entity is upstream, and stay weak on non-Latin text that carries no such entity.
